summary: Across 127.1 minutes and 11 completed experiments, the bounded slowest-five list contains four synthesis-only entries and one compute-bound entry. The recorded compute-task idle indicator is false, so the report-time idle GPU snapshot is not treated as compute-task waste.
bottlenecks_identified: The bounded timing evidence identifies only one of the two compute-bound experiments in the slowest-five list, so a complete compute-bound ranking and the cause of the 16.97-minute transition run cannot be established.
Experiment-level durations have no phase breakdown, leaving the cause of the longest recorded paths unresolved.
No task-correlated model-concurrency record is present, so DualGPURunner selection cannot be audited.
improvements_suggested: Emit phase-level timing receipts for planning, synthesis, validation, artifact writing, and closeout so slow stages can be targeted.
Add dependency-aware parallel dispatch for independent synthesis-only work after timing receipts confirm safe overlap.
Record GPU utilization against each compute-bound task instead of relying on a report-time snapshot.
Record concurrent model count and runner choice, selecting DualGPURunner only when at least two models are loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add phase-level timing receipts to every experiment.
Capture task-correlated GPU and model-concurrency telemetry, with DualGPURunner selected only for parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: The available data supports a bounded wall-time ranking but not causal attribution: the only named compute-bound entry in the slowest-five list is the 16.97-minute transition run, while the other compute-bound experiment is outside that list. Without task-correlated concurrency telemetry or a measured counterfactual, neither a DualGPURunner miss nor savings above 0 percent can be justified.
